sections.html:
Gloucester sits on the lower Middle Peninsula, with the York River along its south edge and the Chesapeake Bay to the east. The seat is Gloucester Courthouse. About a quarter of the county's 288 square miles is water, so many parcels back up to tidal creeks, marsh or river frontage, and buyers ask about flooding and insurance almost at once.

Population stood at 38,711 in 2020 and is estimated at 40,097 for 2025. There were 17,049 housing units in 2020, 9.2% of them vacant, and owners lived in 79.8% of occupied homes. Commuters to the Peninsula cross the York River on the George P. Coleman Memorial Bridge, which carries U.S. 17.

sections.h2: Real estate tax rate and assessments
sections.html:
The 2026 rate on the Treasurer's page is $0.583 for each $100 of assessed value. Values are set at full fair market value, and the law requires a fresh reassessment every three years; the county lists documents for rounds in 2023 and 2026. Staff also list and appraise new construction from building permits.

Duties split between two desks. The Department of Real Estate Assessment sets values from its office at 6489 Main Street, Suite 126, phone 804-693-1325. The Treasurer collects, at 804-693-2141. The department uses mass appraisal, so it follows sales and market shifts rather than deciding values on its own.

Gloucester bills the year in halves.

InstallmentDue dateIf unpaid
FirstJune 3010 percent penalty on July 1, plus 10 percent annual interest
SecondDecember 5 (December 7 in 2026)Penalty after the due date

First-half bills go out in early June and second-half bills in early November. This year the December date shifted to December 7 because the 5th lands on a weekend. Paying the whole year by June 30 is allowed. When a mortgage company escrows your tax, you still answer for making sure it is paid. E-billing is available too; the Treasurer's page explains how to enroll.

Begin by asking the Real Estate Assessment office for an administrative review. Either the owner or an authorized agent can file the county's application, and the cutoff is printed on your reassessment notice, so locate that notice first.

Still unhappy after the review? Apply to the Board of Equalization, five citizens appointed by the Circuit Court. You may skip ahead to the board, though the department resolves most disagreements itself. A petition to the Circuit Court is the final rung, and the Clerk answers at 804-693-2502.

Seniors and disabled owners seeking tax relief apply through the Commissioner of the Revenue at 804-693-3451, between February 1 and May 1.

The Treasurer publishes delinquent lists. Real estate with tax owing for more than two years as of December 31 can be sold at public auction through the bill in equity process in the Virginia Code, and the county names Taxing Authority Consulting Services, P.C. as a firm handling that work.

Sellers should know the Code puts the real estate tax lien first in line, with penalties and interest counted as part of it, until the county is paid. The settlement agent deducts what is owed from your proceeds. Request the Treasurer's payoff number well before the signing appointment.

sections.h2: Water, old deeds and what buyers check
sections.html:
Low lots near creeks draw questions, so prepare answers.

  • Check crawl spaces and the area under porches for moisture.
  • Learn the age of the septic system and the well on rural parcels.
  • Save receipts for roof and drainage work; buyers like proof.

Gloucester dates to 1651, and old deeds can mention parishes and landmarks that no longer exist. An inherited parcel deserves an early request to the Circuit Court clerk for the chain of title, before a title company finds a gap mid-contract. A tornado struck Page Middle School on April 16, 2011, a reminder that storm history is part of the local record, and an insurance agent can tell you how that affects a quote on your address.

Because the county revalues every three years, the best moment to list can depend on where you are in the cycle. The 2026 reassessment is the newest one on the county's document list, and a notice from it carries the deadline for asking for a review. Thinking of selling soon? Read that notice first. If you think the value runs high, challenge it while the window is open, because any buyer and lender will see that same figure.

Value changes also follow construction. Staff pick up new building permits, so a finished addition or a new garage may be added to the record even between general reassessments. Mention improvements, with permits, to a buyer so nothing in the records surprises them later.

sections.h2: What to bring and who to call
sections.html:
Different questions go to different desks, and a short list saves return trips.

  • Value or review questions: Real Estate Assessment, 6489 Main Street, Suite 126, 804-693-1325. Bring the reassessment notice and your parcel details.
  • Balances, receipts and e-billing: the Treasurer, 804-693-2141. Have your account number ready.
  • Relief for seniors or disabled owners: Commissioner of the Revenue, 804-693-3451.
  • Court appeals: Circuit Court Clerk, 804-693-2502.

Phone first when you can. A short call usually tells you which form or which date applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How tax is split at closing
sections.html:
When a house changes hands between installments, someone has to carry the months in between. Your contract sets the split; the settlement agent turns it into line items. A seller who has already paid the June installment is normally repaid by the buyer for the months after closing; a seller who has not yet paid the December installment normally gives the buyer a credit for the months before closing. Check the proration line before signing and question any figure that looks off.

With an escrow account, your servicer may already have paid an installment for you. Ask the servicer for a payoff statement that shows the escrow balance, because the refund of that account arrives separately after the loan is paid off.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed, step by step
sections.html:
Owners here often hold inherited waterfront or rural parcels, older homes needing work, or houses where tax slipped past the June 30 or December 5 dates. A tidy order of operations helps.

  1. Call the Treasurer at 804-693-2141 and ask for the balance on each installment, including penalty and interest.
  2. If you doubt your value, call the assessment office before the notice deadline and ask about an administrative review.
  3. Check with the Commissioner of the Revenue on whether relief or use status ends once the parcel sells.
  4. Send the written figure to the title company, which will pay it from your proceeds at closing.

Cash Home Buyers CA buys Gloucester houses as-is. That route drops the repair list and the wait on a buyer's loan, though any unpaid tax is still taken from the proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 real estate tax rate in Gloucester County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page shows $0.583 per $100 of assessed value for 2026. Real estate is assessed at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: When are Gloucester County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 30 and December 5. In 2026 the December date moved to December 7 because December 5 falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying late in Gloucester County?
faqs.a: The county charges a 10 percent penalty after the due date, plus interest at 10 percent a year on unpaid balances.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Gloucester County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Start with an administrative review at the Real Estate Assessment office, then the Board of Equalization, then the Circuit Court. The reassessment notice lists the deadlines.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gloucester County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Treasurer first.
